findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Trace mitral regurgitation, physiological. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
echo.impression: Structurally near-normal heart with a benign incidental finding.

findings.finding: Impaired: Trail Making Test B below the 5th percentile with set-shifting errors; Stroop interference impaired; perseverative errors on card sorting.
Letter fluency reduced (8 F-words), category fluency low average.
Impaired emotion recognition (Ekman faces, 38/60) and faux pas detection; Frontal Behavioral Inventory (son) 22/72.
Free recall reduced (RAVLT delayed 6/15) with recognition 13/15: a retrieval pattern.
Fluent speech, normal grammar and repetition; confrontation naming within normal limits.
Preserved: complex figure copy and line orientation within normal limits.
Mild ideomotor apraxia of the right hand: 3/5 complex hand postures reproduced to command; left hand 5/5.
Right-hand graphesthesia mildly impaired (4/5 numbers identified); left hand intact. No alien limb phenomenon observed during testing.

output.impression: 1. Executive and social-cognition impairment with reduced letter fluency. 2. Retrieval-pattern memory deficit with preserved recognition. 3. Mild right-hand ideomotor apraxia and right-hand graphesthesia impairment. 4. Language and visuospatial function preserved; mild anxiety without depression. The profile is executive and social-cognitive predominant with relative sparing of memory recognition, consistent with a frontal-network syndrome, with early right-sided cortical (praxis and sensory) signs.

findings.finding: Asymmetric left hemisphere hypometabolism: left orbitofrontal and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex 20-26% below the cerebellar reference; left parietal cortex 14% and left anterior temporal 12% below.
Relatively preserved: borderline right frontal reduction (8%); right parietal and temporal within normal limits.
Left posterior parietal mildly reduced uptake (asymmetric). Right posterior parietal normal. Posterior cingulate preserved bilaterally.

output.impression: 1. Markedly asymmetric left frontal hypometabolism with milder left parietal and anterior temporal involvement. 2. Right hemisphere relatively preserved; posterior cingulate preserved bilaterally. Pattern consistent with an asymmetric frontotemporal lobar degeneration metabolic profile.

findings.finding: Reduced perfusion of the left orbitofrontal and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, with milder left parietal and anterior temporal reduction.
Normal posterior cingulate and precuneus perfusion bilaterally.

output.impression: 1. Asymmetric left frontal hypoperfusion with milder left parietal and anterior temporal involvement. 2. Posterior cingulate preserved. Pattern consistent with asymmetric frontotemporal hypoperfusion.

output.interpretation: Plasma progranulin 42 ng/mL, below the assay reference range.

findings.result: No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant

output.impression: 1. Heterozygous pathogenic GRN c.709-1G>A splice-site variant, the variant previously identified in this patient by cascade testing. 2. No C9orf72 repeat expansion and no pathogenic MAPT variant. Post-test genetic counselling, including the implications for at-risk relatives, is recommended.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Son's account of impulsive disposal of her daughter's photographs, withdrawal from friends, emotional blunting and rigid routines, with medication-management errors and an executive MoCA pattern
action_criteria.label: Structured informant history and bedside cognitive screen scored against the Rascovsky features
action_criteria.rationale: The diagnosis of bvFTD rests on the behavioural features obtained from an informant; the screen documents the cognitive profile.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Executive and social-cognition deficits with preserved recognition memory, plus mild right-hand apraxia and graphesthesia impairment
action_criteria.label: Neuropsychological battery including executive and social-cognition measures
action_criteria.rationale: Quantifies the executive and social-cognition profile and the relative sparing of memory and visuospatial function.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No reversible metabolic, endocrine or inflammatory cause
action_criteria.label: Reversible-cause blood tests: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, ESR, CRP
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory contributors before attributing decline to neurodegeneration.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Asymmetric left frontal and mild left parietal atrophy with preserved posterior cortex and normal white matter
action_criteria.label: MRI brain without contrast, dementia protocol
action_criteria.rationale: Shows the frontal and anterior temporal atrophy pattern and excludes structural and vascular causes.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Asymmetric left frontal and parietal hypometabolism or hypoperfusion with posterior cingulate sparing
action_criteria.label: FDG-PET when the structural picture is unresolved
action_criteria.rationale: Frontal and anterior temporal hypometabolism with posterior sparing supports FTD over AD.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on the phenotypes and genetics of familial FTD
action_criteria.label: Literature search on GRN-associated FTD phenotypes (optional)
action_criteria.rationale: General evidence only; it does not change the work-up of this patient.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present and the functional decline, and that a known pathogenic GRN variant in a patient who meets the clinical criteria places her in the definite category.

Explain why grief or an adjustment reaction does not explain the picture: a qualitatively new syndrome of blunted affect, rigid routines and impulsive acts, with errors she denies, asymmetric left frontal atrophy and right-hand apraxia and cortical sensory signs.
Name the early right-sided apraxia and cortical sensory signs as part of the corticobasal spectrum seen with GRN, and plan follow-up of motor, language and praxis function.

Address safety: she should no longer manage her daughter's medicines alone given the errors; arrange supervision of finances, review driving, and discuss lasting power of attorney and advance care planning while she can take part.
Offer genetic counselling for the family, including her son (50% risk) if he wishes to consider predictive testing, and discuss GRN research cohorts and clinical trials now that she is symptomatic.
Arrange caregiver support for her son, who is caring for both his mother and his sister, with a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not part of the FTD work-up; FDG-PET, or perfusion SPECT where FDG-PET is unavailable, is the functional study when one is needed.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

accepted: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, GRN-associated (with early corticobasal syndrome features)

differential.key_features: For: daughter's illness and caregiver stress; anxiety. Against: absent grief rather than excessive grief, new rigid routines and impulsive acts, errors she denies, executive deficits, asymmetric frontal atrophy and right-hand cortical signs; no depressive syndrome.
Against: a pathogenic GRN variant with a concordant syndrome, retrieval-pattern memory with preserved recognition, and frontal-predominant atrophy and hypometabolism with posterior cingulate sparing.
Against: no gaze palsy, postural instability or axial rigidity.

key_clinical_evidence: Known pathogenic GRN splice-site variant (c.709-1G>A), with a daughter affected at 34 and a mother who died of dementia at 62.

Son's account over 10 months: emotional blunting toward her daughter's decline, giving away family photographs without discussion, rigid routines and withdrawal from friends, with medication-management errors she denies.
Neuropsychology: executive and social-cognition deficits with preserved recognition memory; mild right-hand ideomotor apraxia and graphesthesia impairment.
MRI: asymmetric left frontal and mild left parietal atrophy with preserved posterior cortex, concordant with the right-sided cortical signs.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Grief and caregiver stress do not produce absent grief, rigid routines, impulsive acts and asymmetric atrophy; in a known GRN carrier at the expected age this is symptom onset.
red_herrings.data_point: Son initially attributed the changes to grief and caregiver stress
red_herrings.intended_effect: Could mislead toward an adjustment reaction.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A MoCA of 24/30 often understates bvFTD; the informant history and neuropsychology carry the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Could mislead toward dismissing the son's concerns.

clinical_assessment.impression: 5 of the 6 Rascovsky features are present on informant history and examination (disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy, compulsive routines and an executive-predominant profile), with documented decline in daily function. This meets possible bvFTD; imaging and neuropsychological testing decide whether it is probable. Memory and visuospatial function are relatively preserved on the bedside screen.

Progranulin (GRN) associated frontotempo.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. C9orf72 expansions and GRN and MAPT variants cause most familial FTD; counselling precedes any genetic test and any predictive testing of relatives. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: Required core: structured informant assessment, neuropsychological battery, reversible-cause blood tests and brain MRI. Optional: FDG-PET or SPECT, literature search.
metadata.notes: bvFTD in a 59-year-old woman with a known pathogenic GRN splice-site variant, with early right-sided corticobasal features (right-hand apraxia and graphesthesia) concordant with asymmetric left frontal and parietal atrophy. Key teaching: in a known carrier, a qualitatively new syndrome at the expected age is symptom onset rather than grief, and the asymmetric phenotype is typical of GRN.

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. P is a 59-year-old retired pharmacist who is a known carrier of a pathogenic GRN splice site mutation (c.709-1G>A), identified 2 years ago through cascade family genetic testing after her daughter was diagnosed with early-onset FTD-GRN at age 34. Her mother died of dementia at age 62, retrospectively consistent with FTD. Her brother, also a carrier, is currently asymptomatic at age 61. She presents today with her son, who has been increasingly concerned about behavioral changes over the past 10 months. She is aware of her genetic status and is actively monitoring herself for symptom onset. She retired from pharmacy 2 years ago, partly precipitated by her daughter's diagnosis. Her son describes a pattern that he initially attributed to grief and caregiver stress related to her daughter's illness. However, over the past several months, he has noted behaviors that concern him: she has been making repetitive errors in managing her daughter's complex medication schedule — forgetting steps she herself established — and then insisting she completed them. She has become emotionally blunted in a way her son finds striking — she does not visibly grieve her daughter's deteriorating condition. She recently gave away a collection of her daughter's childhood photographs without discussing it with any family members, causing significant family distress. She has developed a highly rigid daily routine and becomes irritable when it is disrupted. She has stopped calling her friends of 30+ years. She continues to function in basic ADLs and manages her own finances, but her son is concerned about subtle errors.

neurological_exam.additional: Son reports: she has been making repetitive errors managing her daughter's medical affairs (forgetting medication schedules she set up herself). She has become emotionally blunted — does not cry at her daughter's decline, which the son finds remarkable. She recently gave away her daughter's childhood photographs without consultation. She has become quite rigid about daily routines. She is a known carrier of a pathogenic GRN variant (identified on presymptomatic genetic testing initiated after her daughter's diagnosis), is now 59, and is concerned about symptom onset.
